# Backend Collection Processing

Use only the rules that apply to the current consumer task.

## Contents

- [Collection processing and bounded deadlock retries](#collection-processing-and-bounded-deadlock-retries)

## Collection processing and bounded deadlock retries

Keep filtering, ordering, paging, and projection server-side with validated paging defaults and filter and order keys checked segment by segment against [Filterable] and [Orderable] view models, while retrying only recognized relational deadlock victims within the configured collection-processing bound.

## Preferred approach

Use `ICollectionProcessingService` or `IHttpCollectionProcessingService` to apply filtering, ordering, paging, and projection without materializing early. Configure `NewHeap:PlatformCommon:Settings:CollectionProcessingDefaultItemsPerPage` and `CollectionProcessingDefaultMaxItemsPerPage` when the compatible defaults of 20 and 1000 do not fit the endpoint. Both values must be at least one, and the default page size cannot exceed the default maximum. An endpoint-specific maximum passed to `GetCollectionRequestModel` still takes precedence.

Configure `NewHeap:PlatformCommon:Settings:CollectionProcessingDeadlockMaxAttempts` when the default maximum of five attempts does not match the application's operational policy. The value counts the initial command, must be at least one, and applies independently to the count and item-materialization commands.

Let collection processing retry only provider-confirmed deadlock victims: SQL Server error `1205` and PostgreSQL SQLSTATE `40P01`. Keep the query read-only and idempotent. Other database errors, exhausted deadlocks, invalid configuration, and cancellation remain exceptions so callers and operators retain the original failure.

For opt-in table field selection, branch only when `NhFieldSelectionService.HasSelection(Request)` is true. Keep the existing controller path when `fields` is absent, even if `format` is supplied. Use an explicit scalar member-initializer projection with `[Selectable]` fields. Apply row/division restrictions to the source first. Add `[FieldAccess(Roles = "role-a,role-b")]` for role OR checks or a named ASP.NET policy with an authorized resource context for custom checks. Roles and policy, and multiple attributes, must all succeed. Per-row access checks require a separate contract or row-scoped query; the field-selection service does not execute asynchronous per-row policies.

Expose authorized descriptors through `DescribeAsync<TView>` on a protected discovery endpoint; fetch them when opening table settings. Do not cache descriptors or selected responses across users/divisions. Recheck access for every request, and reject unavailable fields and filter/order probes before querying. Search only authorized searchable fields. Selection metadata reports requested and canonical returned fields even for empty pages. Use `ToActionResult` for JSON or explicit `format=messagepack`, with JSON as the measured default. The compatibility MessagePack writer preserves names and scalar browser semantics; benchmark before claiming a speed improvement.

`FieldAccess` only protects requests that opt in with `fields`. Removing `fields` deliberately retains legacy behavior. It is not a security boundary for an existing unrestricted endpoint; applying the policy everywhere requires a separate migration of that endpoint. See the executable project controller, `ProjectTableViewModel`, and the sample field-selection guide.

Treat a filter key as a path over the view model, not over the entity. Collection processing checks every dotted segment of every filter node, including `Ands` and `Ors`, on both the attribute-based and the options-based path: the first segment must be a `[Filterable]` property of the view model, and every later segment a `[Filterable]` property of the view-model type the previous segment reaches, or of its element type when that segment is a collection (`tasks{any}.title`). A key that names an unknown or unmarked member at any step fails with `InvalidFilterCollectionResultException`, which the base controllers return as `400`. To allow a nested filter, mark the navigation or collection and the nested view-model members that may be filtered; leave entity-only columns, such as credentials, tokens and internal identifiers, off the view model or unmarked. A configured `WithFilterable(key, selector)` allows exactly its key and may reach any entity member, so use it deliberately. SPM-034 shows accepted owner and task keys and rejected entity-only keys on SQL Server and PostgreSQL.

Check order keys the same way. Every dotted segment of every `+` part of an order key must be an `[Orderable]` property of the view model or of the view-model type the previous segment reaches, on both the attribute-based and the options-based path. A step into a collection names one member of its items behind a lower-case `{first:asc}`, `{first:desc}`, `{last:asc}` or `{last:desc}` token (`tasks.{first:asc}deadline`). Only the matched property names and tokens reach Dynamic LINQ, never the client's text. Any other order key is skipped, as unknown order keys always were, and the request keeps its other order keys or the default order: a key that continues behind a scalar such as `creationDateTime.year == 2001 ? secret.length : 0` therefore cannot order rows by a column the view model does not expose, and a stale sort key from a client does not fail the request. A configured `WithOrderable(key, selector)` allows exactly its key. SPM-034 orders by `ownerUser.email` on PostgreSQL, translates that ordering for SQL Server and PostgreSQL, and ignores a key behind `creationDateTime`, whose SQL keeps the default order.

Keep the filter structure stable across requests. Collection processing numbers new lambda parameters `x1`, `x2`, and so on within each filter collection, including nested filters. AND/OR parts that refer to the same variable keep sharing its parameter. The numbering restarts for each collection, so EF can reuse compilation when only filter values change.

## Avoid

- Giving dynamically constructed lambda parameters random names; EF includes those names in its query-cache hash.
- Matching localized provider message text to identify a deadlock.
- Retrying every `DbException` or hiding an exhausted retry as a successful empty collection.
- Putting writes or other side effects in a collection query or materialization callback.
- Adding controller-local retry loops around collection processing.
- Repeating paging constants in controllers or HTTP request parsing instead of using the platform-common settings.
- Configuring a default page size above the configured default maximum.
- Using a value below one or treating the setting as additional retries after the initial attempt.
- Treating `[Selectable]` as implicit authorization, or enforcing field visibility only in the browser.
- Filtering, sorting or searching denied fields, or materializing full entities before selected projection.
- Marking a navigation `[Filterable]` and expecting it to open the whole related entity; only the nested view-model members marked `[Filterable]` can be filtered.
- Exposing an entity-only column for filtering through a configured selector without treating that selector as part of the public contract.
- Passing a client order key, or any part of it, to Dynamic LINQ without checking every segment against `[Orderable]` view-model members, or sorting a client column that the view model does not mark `[Orderable]`.
- Interpreting empty/invalid `fields` as permission to return the legacy full model.
- Assuming MessagePack is faster without measuring allocations, encoding, decoding and end-to-end latency.

## Verification

Verify the compatible paging defaults, configured paging values, invalid paging combinations, the default five-attempt retry bound, a configured lower retry bound, immediate propagation of non-deadlock failures, and retry of SQL Server `1205` and PostgreSQL `40P01` during both count and item materialization. Run the normal collection flow against SQL Server and PostgreSQL, and keep filtering, ordering, and paging server-side.

Run `FieldSelectionTests` and `ProjectFieldSelectionSamplesTests` for the opt-in branch, alias/falsy/null values, resource policies, forbidden queries and JSON/MessagePack parity. The provider tests run on one shared SQL Server and one shared PostgreSQL container per test process, each test in an empty database of its own. Translation-only tests do not replace actual execution evidence. Run the collection encoding benchmark in Release from its project directory and keep JSON the default unless representative end-to-end measurements justify a change.

Run `CollectionFilterPathValidationTests` for SQL Server and PostgreSQL: allowed nested navigation and collection keys execute, keys that reach an unmarked or entity-only member through a `[Filterable]` navigation or collection are rejected, also inside `Ands` and `Ors`, on both the attribute-based and the options-based path. Run `ProjectNestedFilterSamplesTests` and `CollectionAndProjectionSamplesTests.NestedFilterKeysTranslateOnEachProvider` for the sample.

Run `CollectionOrderPathValidationTests` for SQL Server and PostgreSQL: allowed scalar, navigation, concatenated and collection-token order keys execute, and keys that continue behind a scalar, reach an unmarked or entity-only member, carry operators or use another token spelling leave the default order in place on both paths. Run `ProjectNestedFilterSamplesTests.NestedOrderKeysReachOnlyOrderableViewMembers` and `CollectionAndProjectionSamplesTests.NestedOrderKeysTranslateOnEachProvider` for the sample.

Run `CollectionQueryCacheTests` for SQL Server and PostgreSQL translation and execution, including repeated equality, nested any/all filters, combined AND/OR groups, unique sequential parameter names, changed values, and count/item query reuse through both attribute- and options-based filtering. `CollectionAndProjectionSamplesTests.StatusFiltersReuseCompilationAcrossRequests` demonstrates the same cache behavior with the sample project status filter.
